transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Hi, Barbara is it?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Hi, yes.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: I'm Eliza, nice to meet you. How are you today?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, I'm well thanks.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: That's good, you make it here okay?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, it was alright, traffic was a bit slow as always.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Yeah, did you catch the bus or drive down here?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: No, I drove. It's a bit of a pain to park around here though, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Yeah, it is, but it's alright, it's easier than catching the bus. No worries, you feeling okay here at the moment?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, alright thanks.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: I'm just going to have a glass of water, would you like one?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yes please, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: It's nice and cool in here, at least with the really hot day outside we can relax in the air conditioner.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: So just before we get started, I just want to ask, is it okay if I take a couple of notes during our interview?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, absolutely.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: You're okay with that?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, no problem.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: And just want you to know as well that everything that we discuss here today is just between the two of us, so I won't be talking about this case to anybody else. Obviously you tell me what you want to tell me, and when you're comfortable you can continue more. I'll just be asking you a couple of questions, and then we'll just go from there.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Okay, perfect, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: So tell me, what brings you here today?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: So a couple of weeks ago, my boyfriend and I went to a music festival together, and we were in a group of people, it was up in Byron Bay, and obviously as with all music festivals, there were sniffer dogs and police squads around, sussing out people with drugs, and I wasn't worried at all because I knew that I didn't have anything on me, that I hadn't brought anything in, so I pretty much just walked straight past them and I got sniffed out by one of the dogs. And a policeman came over and he took, he was searching me and he found a bag of drugs in my jacket pocket, which I just had no idea where it came from because I knew that I hadn't taken anything in, and I told them that, and I denied everything, and I told them I had no idea what they were, or where they came from, or how they got into my jacket, and they just thought I was being really evasive and non-cooperative and threatened to take me to the station and keep me overnight, but essentially they just charged me with possession and issued me a court attendance notice and let me go.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Were you alone at the time?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: No, I was with my boyfriend and a couple of other friends, oh do you mean when I was talking to the police?

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Yeah, absolutely.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, I was just, they pulled me aside, but yeah, I was at the festival with a bunch of people, including my boyfriend.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, and then when I got home, they, he told me what he'd done, which is essentially taken his bag of drugs that he brought into the festival with him and put them in my jacket when I wasn't looking, as soon as he saw the sniffer dogs.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: And he didn't tell you this at the time?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: No, I had no idea that he was even planning on taking drugs or planning on bringing anything in, he never mentioned it, I really had no idea about anything at all, and yeah, like I was really angry at him obviously, as you would be, but then, you know, I kind of more or less agreed to take the fall for him.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Is there any reason that you took the fall for him? They weren't his drugs to begin with?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, I don't know, I think it's because, I mean I've been with him for a while now and I obviously care about him a lot and he is in his final year of a law degree, he's about to graduate, he's got clerkship lined up over the summer and he's, yeah, him and his family are just really good to me, like I live rent free in an apartment that his parents own in the city and, like I'm, sorry, I'm in uni myself and he's supporting me financially throughout my uni degree, so yeah, I just, yeah, I'm just prepared to do pretty much whatever I need to do to keep him and his family out of the whole thing.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Right, so you obviously care a lot about his future, seeing as he's in his last year of his law degree.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Is there any other reason as to why you're wanting to take the fall for him? Because I'm assuming you probably also have future prospects.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, I do, but there's something else about his family that I just need you to promise like no one's going to hear about this at all.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Of course, that's my lock between the two of us, I want confidentiality.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Okay, because this is not something I want to get out at all. His dad is a prominent former politician and the fallout from this would just be, like the media fallout would just be huge and his dad is also currently facing corruption charges with like following an ICAC inquiry, so yeah, I just want to keep them out of that for that reason and also his family's told me that they'd look after me if I took the fall for this and it's just a way for me to feel like I have their approval for this.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: The approval is obviously something that you want.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, I do.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Do you feel entirely comfortable with this decision that you're making?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yes, yeah, yeah.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Okay, so you mentioned that he was the one that slipped the drugs into your bag at the festival.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, my jacket.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Into your jacket, sorry, yeah, jacket. Just tell me a little bit more about that, do you know how many drugs there were at the time, who was around you, that sort of thing?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: To be honest, I didn't really look that closely at the bag, but I would think there was maybe eight to ten pills in there.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Eight to ten, okay.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah, I'm not quite sure, I don't even know what they were, I just saw the police take it out of the bag, I mean take it out of my jacket and yeah.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Okay, do you know when your court notice is due?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: I think it's in 28 days.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: 28 days, okay. Alright, is there anything else that you need to let me know about or tell me before I can?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: No, I think that's, I mean that's everything, yeah.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Okay, great. Alright, well, I'll have a look at all the information that you've given me, I'll be able to write up a letter of engagement and then give you a letter of advice and then we can go from there. Obviously, you can continue thinking about your decision and if it's the right path that you want to take. Obviously, it'll be a discussion between two of us, I'll give you my advice and then you can take that away and think about that and we'll go from there.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Can I, just before we depart, can I just clarify a couple more details?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: So, you're Barbara Jennings?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: That's correct, double N-I-N-G-S?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: And it's 19A Woolgoogah Street, North Sydney?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yep.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Wonderful, okay. Is there any other questions you need to ask me today?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: No, no, I think that's fine, yeah.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: Okay, wonderful. Well, you can go and enjoy the sunshine.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Lawyer 1
transcript.text: No problem. Lovely to see you.

summary: The initial consultation involved Lawyer Eliza and Client Barbara Jennings, who is facing charges of drug possession after allegedly taking responsibility for drugs that her boyfriend concealed in her jacket at a music festival. Barbara explained that she accepted the blame because of her relationship with her boyfriend and the financial and personal support offered by his family. She expressed significant concern about possible media exposure due to her boyfriend's father's political involvement and ongoing legal matters. Lawyer Eliza assured Barbara of confidentiality, outlined upcoming steps—such as preparing a letter of engagement and providing legal advice—and confirmed Barbara's personal information. The meeting concluded with Barbara being encouraged to fully consider her options regarding how to proceed.
action_items: Prepare and send a letter of engagement to Barbara Jennings.
Draft and provide a letter of legal advice to Barbara.
Barbara to carefully review her situation and decide whether to proceed with taking responsibility for the drug possession charge.
